pass_b_english: All those being initiated will hear the same message from the mystagogues. Speaking as moved by one Spirit, they do not argue with one another in words but instead harmoniously proclaim the divine doctrines. They announce the mystery of Christ covertly, as befits the sacred instruction of newcomers. This, I believe, is what was meant by 'Then they shall declare judgment.' For the people of Israel had named the law given through Moses as judgment, and thus it is quite reasonable that they would oppose the evangelical and saving proclamation by setting it against the law, calling this proclamation judgment through these very actions. For the true righteous judgment, and the power of the legislation that pleases God, is not more clearly seen in the shadow of the law, but shines forth in the proclamation of the holy mystagogues who are the new leaders. Those who have learned from Christ the judgment—that is, the will of God the Father—have proclaimed this same judgment to us by living in accordance with it. Who stirred up righteousness from the east? He summoned it to walk at his feet, and it goes forth. We ought not to marvel at the God who possesses all merely because of the mere greatness of his works, but also because of the benefits he bestows, through which he makes manifest his own tranquility. For he has saved those upon the earth, utterly destroyed the human race and death, brought forth corruption, and stripped the devil of his malicious abundance. He has abolished the devil's tyranny together with its powers, yet he has made known through faith the defeat of sin that once tyrannized over us, having put it to shame. Indeed, all these things have been set right through Christ.
